# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 90 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 90 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_090_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — Mountains Five through Eight

**1** "The fifth mountain — green-grassed but rough and rocky — represents those who believed and are genuine in their faith, but are hard to get along with. They're presumptuous and opinionated, wanting to know everything but actually understanding very little. **2** Their arrogance has driven wisdom away from them — rashness and recklessness have taken its place. That's why their type is like the rocky parts of the mountain. **3** But God isn't angry with them, because at core they're good people — they just have a stubborn streak. If they learn to hold themselves back and embrace genuine humility, repentance is available to them. **4** "The sixth mountain — full of large and small cracks — represents those who believed: those in the small cracks are quarrelsome types, weak in faith; those in the large cracks are aggressively wicked and self-important. Repentance is still possible for them, but it won't be easy — they'll only make it through with great difficulty." **5** "The seventh mountain — covered in cheerful green grass where animals of every kind grazed and birds came to rest — represents those who believed and are genuinely innocent and pure-hearted. They were never torn by internal conflict; they always lived in joy. **6** "The eighth mountain — overflowing with springs that gave water to creatures of every kind — represents the apostles and teachers who proclaimed the name of the Son of God. They completed their mission and then fell asleep in the power and holiness of the Son of God."

---

*PNEUMA renders the character portraits of mountains 5-6 with direct contemporary language; mountains 7-8 ascend to the ideal — innocent joy and apostolic fountainhead.*
